/*
    Canteen: module settings table
    Date   : 2026-10-23

    WHAT IT ADDS
      HR_CMS_Config - the canteen module's own settings, one row for the whole installation (the row is
      pinned to ConfigId = 1 by a CHECK constraint, so there can never be a second one to disagree with
      the first). It starts with a single setting:

        MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore   how far back the Meal Session screen lets an ordering deadline be set.
                                   1 (the default) = the deadline may fall on the day of the meal or the
                                   day before. 2 = also two days before, and so on up to 7.

      This is NOT when ordering closes - that is per meal session (HR_CMS_MealSession.OrderCutoffTime /
      OrderCutoffDaysBefore, set on the Meal Session screen). This is only how many choices that screen's
      "Cutoff Day" list offers. It lives here rather than in appsettings.json so it can be changed without
      touching a config file or restarting the API: the screen reads this row every time it is opened.

    HOW TO CHANGE IT
      Let the kitchen be told up to three days ahead:

        UPDATE dbo.HR_CMS_Config
           SET MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore = 3, ModifiedDate = GETDATE(), ModifiedById = 1
         WHERE ConfigId = 1;

      Anyone on the Meal Session screen sees the longer list the next time they open it - no deploy, no
      restart. Lowering it again never invalidates a meal session already saved with a longer notice:
      that session keeps its deadline and still saves, it just cannot be moved further back.
      0 to 7 only - CK_HR_CMS_MealSession_OrderCutoffDaysBefore will not store a deadline beyond 7 days.

    Run BEFORE deploying the code. Idempotent - safe to run more than once.
    SQL Server 2014 compatible.
*/

SET NOCOUNT ON;

IF OBJECT_ID(N'[dbo].[HR_CMS_Config]', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE [dbo].[HR_CMS_Config]
    (
        [ConfigId]                 INT      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_HR_CMS_Config PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED,
        [MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] INT      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_CMS_Config_MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore DEFAULT (1),
        [CreateDate]               DATETIME NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_CMS_Config_CreateDate DEFAULT (GETDATE()),
        [CreatedById]              BIGINT   NOT NULL,
        [ModifiedDate]             DATETIME NULL,
        [ModifiedById]             BIGINT   NULL,
        -- One installation, one row: no second row can exist to contradict this one.
        CONSTRAINT CK_HR_CMS_Config_SingleRow CHECK ([ConfigId] = 1),
        -- The same ceiling the meal session's own deadline is held to.
        CONSTRAINT CK_HR_CMS_Config_MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore CHECK ([MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)
    )

    PRINT N'HR_CMS_Config created.';
END
GO

-- The settings row. Seeded with 1 - the day of the meal, or the day before - which is what the code
-- falls back to if this row is ever missing, so seeding it changes nothing by itself.
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM [dbo].[HR_CMS_Config] WHERE [ConfigId] = 1)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO [dbo].[HR_CMS_Config] ([ConfigId], [MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore], [CreatedById])
    VALUES (1, 1, 1);

    PRINT N'HR_CMS_Config seeded with MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore = 1.';
END
GO

SELECT [ConfigId],
       [MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore],
       [The Cutoff Day list offers] = CASE [MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore]
                                          WHEN 0 THEN N'the day of the meal only'
                                          WHEN 1 THEN N'the day of the meal, or the day before'
                                          ELSE N'the day of the meal, up to ' + CAST([MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] AS NVARCHAR(10)) + N' days before'
                                      END,
       [ModifiedDate]
FROM [dbo].[HR_CMS_Config];
GO

content.text:
The maximum now lives in the database. Here's the shape.

## New table

`Migration_CanteenConfig_20261023.sql` creates `HR_CMS_Config` — one row for the whole installation, pinned by a CHECK so a second row can never exist to disagree with the first:

```sql
[ConfigId]                 INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
[MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] INT NOT NULL DEFAULT (1),
CONSTRAINT CK_HR_CMS_Config_SingleRow               CHECK ([ConfigId] = 1),
CONSTRAINT CK_HR_CMS_Config_MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore CHECK ([MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)
```

Changing it is one statement, documented in the script header:

```sql
UPDATE dbo.HR_CMS_Config
   SET MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore = 3, ModifiedDate = GETDATE(), ModifiedById = 1
 WHERE ConfigId = 1;
```

The service reads the row on every call, so the longer list appears the next time anyone opens the screen — no deploy, no restart. The `appsettings.json` key is gone, so there's only one place to look.

**I made it global rather than per-company**, against the usual `HR_FNFConfig` house pattern, because the thing it constrains is global: `HR_CMS_MealSession` has no `CompanyMasterId`, so a per-company maximum would be policing a meal session that every company shares. Say the word if the canteen is heading toward per-company sessions and I'll scope it.

## Wiring

New `ICanteenConfigRepository` / `CanteenConfigRepository` registered in the DAL's `CmsDependencyInjection`, with `HrCmsConfig` mapped in `HrmsystemContext`. `MealSessionService` takes it in place of `IOptions<MealBookingSettings>`; `GetOrderCutoffDayOptions` and the save-time validation are now async off that read. A missing settings row falls back to 1 — the same value the migration seeds — so a database that hasn't been seeded still works rather than collapsing the dropdown to a single choice.

**No frontend change.** The dropdown was already built from whatever `GetOrderCutoffDayOptions` returns, which is exactly the seam this needed; only the source behind that endpoint moved.

## Run order

`Migration_CanteenConfig_20261023.sql` before `Migration_CanteenMealSessionOrderCutoff_20261023.sql` (the cutoff script's header now points at the config row), then `Update_CanteenMealSession_OrderCutoff_20261023.sql` once you have the four real deadlines — still the one outstanding item.

I also noted down that builds and tests are yours to run, so I won't kick those off again.

# Frontend Changes — Exit Formality Module (new)

Backend is done (API only — no new DB migration; `HR_ExitFormality`/`HR_ExitClearance` and the
`HR_FNFSettlement.ExitFormalityID`/`HR_FNFConfig.RequireExitFormality` columns already exist in the
shared DB, ported from hr_payroll's own migration). No Angular pages exist for this yet — this doc
is the contract to build against.

One screen, one controller (`api/ExitFormality`): the stage between an employee resigning and F&F
opening. Three things must be true before a settlement may be calculated — the exit interview is
recorded, every issued asset is back, and every department has answered — and this screen is where
that gets tracked and verified.

## 1. The three-leg completeness gate

```
Exit Interview        (recorded on this screen)
Asset Return          (recorded in Assets ▸ Asset Return — this screen only READS the balance)
Department Clearance  (5 fixed rows: IT, Finance, Admin, HR, Reporting Manager — recorded here)

All three done  →  IsComplete = true  →  "Create F&F Case" becomes available
```

- **Asset Return is not owned by this screen.** The Asset Return tab is read-only, showing what the
  Assets module already knows (issued minus returned quantity). Tell the user to go record the
  actual return in Assets ▸ Asset Return, then come back and press **Re-check**.
- **A department clearance is "answered" once it's `Cleared` OR `Objection Raised` — only `Pending`
  blocks.** An objection does **not** block completion: raising one with a `duesAmount` is how a due
  gets recorded, and it flows into the F&F case as a recovery when the case is created. If
  objections blocked completion, the case could never be created and the money could never be
  collected.
- **An `Objection Raised` row with `duesAmount > 0` requires `duesDescription`.** The API returns
  `400` ("Say what the dues are for...") if you try to save one without it — it becomes the
  description on the resulting F&F recovery line, so an empty one would read as an unexplained
  deduction. A `duesAmount` of `0` does not require a description.
- **The interview counts as done for `Completed`, `Employee Not Available`, or `Skipped`** — not
  just `Completed`. An employee who has already walked out cannot be interviewed; don't gate on
  `Completed` alone or some exits will never complete.
- **The block reason names exactly one thing** — the first outstanding leg, in interview → assets →
  clearance order. Show it as-is; it already reads as an actionable sentence
  (e.g. `"2 asset item(s) are still with the employee. Record the return in Assets > Asset Return."`
  or `"IT Department has not responded yet. (2 departments yet to respond)"`). Don't try to enumerate
  every outstanding item yourself — recompute happens on every Save/Recheck, so the message is
  always current.

## 2. Response envelope & auth

# Canteen — Meal Ordering Deadline

Date: 23-Oct-2026

Every meal session now carries the moment ordering closes for it, set by HR on the Meal Session
screen. Until now that moment was a single number in `appsettings.json`
(`MealBooking.BookingCloseHours = 2`), which closed every meal two hours before it was served —
the same rule for breakfast and for dinner, invisible to HR, and changeable only by editing a
config file and restarting the API.

A canteen does not work that way. Breakfast has to be counted the night before so the kitchen can
shop; lunch is counted the same morning. The deadline is a property of the meal, so it now lives on
the meal.

## 1. Database changes

### 1.1 `HR_CMS_MealSession` — two new columns

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OrderCutoffTime` | `TIME(0)` NOT NULL | the clock time ordering closes |
| `OrderCutoffDaysBefore` | `INT` NOT NULL | which day that clock time falls on: `0` = the day of the meal, `1` = the day before, up to `7` |

Read together they are one deadline. Breakfast ordered "by 11:59 PM the night before" is
`23:59` + `1`. Lunch ordered "by 9:30 in the morning" is `09:30` + `0`.

Both are **NOT NULL by design** — there is no "deadline not configured" state for a meal session to
sit in, because the booking API has to be able to answer "is it too late?" for every meal, every
time.

Two CHECK constraints keep the pair meaningful:

```sql
CK_HR_CMS_MealSession_OrderCutoffDaysBefore
    CHECK ([OrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)

CK_HR_CMS_MealSession_OrderCutoffBeforeStart
    CHECK ([OrderCutoffDaysBefore] > 0 OR [OrderCutoffTime] <= [StartTime])
```

The second one is the rule that matters: **a deadline on the day of the meal can never be after the
meal starts.** Breakfast served 07:30–09:30 cannot be ordered at 08:00 that morning — the food is
already cooked. `07:30` exactly is allowed (it reads as "order before 7:30"); `07:31` is refused. A
deadline on an earlier day is always in time, whatever the clock says, so the constraint only
applies when `OrderCutoffDaysBefore = 0`.

### 1.2 `HR_CMS_Config` — new table

The canteen module's own settings, one row for the whole installation. It starts with one setting:

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfigId` | `INT` PK | always `1` |
| `MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore` | `INT` NOT NULL, default `1` | how far back the Meal Session screen lets a deadline be set |
| `CreateDate` / `CreatedById` / `ModifiedDate` / `ModifiedById` | | audit |

```sql
CK_HR_CMS_Config_SingleRow                CHECK ([ConfigId] = 1)
CK_HR_CMS_Config_MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore CHECK ([MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)
```

`MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore` is **not** when ordering closes — it only decides how many choices the
screen's **Cutoff Day** list offers. At the seeded value of `1`, HR can choose the day of the meal
or the day before. To let a kitchen be told three days ahead:

```sql
UPDATE dbo.HR_CMS_Config
   SET MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore = 3, ModifiedDate = GETDATE(), ModifiedById = 1
 WHERE ConfigId = 1;
```

The screen reads this row every time it is opened, so the longer list appears immediately — no
deploy, no restart. It is held in the database rather than `appsettings.json` for exactly that
reason.

It is global rather than per-company because the thing it governs is global: `HR_CMS_MealSession`
has no `CompanyMasterId`, so a per-company maximum would be policing a meal session that every
company shares. The single-row CHECK means a second, contradicting row can never appear.

### 1.3 Scripts, in run order

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Migration_CanteenConfig_20261023.sql` | creates `HR_CMS_Config`, seeds the row with `1` |
| `Migration_CanteenMealSessionOrderCutoff_20261023.sql` | adds the two columns, backfills them, adds the two CHECKs |
| `Update_CanteenMealSession_OrderCutoff_20261023.sql` | sets HR's real deadlines (preview → `@Apply = 1`) |

All three run **before** the code is deployed, and all three are safe to run more than once.

**The backfill keeps the old behaviour.** Existing rows are filled with `StartTime` minus two hours
— the rule that was in force — rolling to `OrderCutoffDaysBefore = 1` if that crosses midnight. So
on the day this is deployed, nothing changes for any employee; the deadlines only become real when
HR sets them. The backfill is wired inside the second column's `IF NOT EXISTS`, so it runs exactly
once, on the run that creates the columns, and can never overwrite a deadline set since.

The third script is the one that carries the agreed figures, in the same preview-then-apply shape
as `Update_CanteenMealSession_Rates_20261022.sql`. It refuses to apply a same-day deadline that
falls after its meal starts, naming the session, rather than letting the CHECK constraint fail with
a number.

### 1.4 Settings removed from `appsettings.json`

```jsonc
"MealBooking": {
  "BookingCloseHours": 2,    // REMOVED — replaced by the per-session deadline
  "CancelCutoffHours": 24,   // REMOVED — cancelling now stops at that same deadline
  ...
}
```

Nothing about the deadline is in config any more. What remains under `MealBooking` is request
limits (`MaxDatesPerRequest`, `MaxRangeDays`) and the time-zone map.

## 2. Functionality

### 2.1 One deadline for ordering *and* cancelling

`CancelCutoffHours` was a separate 24-hour rule, and against a same-day deadline it was incoherent:
with lunch closing at 09:30 on the day, an employee who booked at 09:29 could never cancel — the
24-hour window had already passed at the moment of booking.

Both now stop at the same moment: **until the deadline you can freely add or drop a meal; after it
the kitchen's count is final.** One rule to explain, and no meal can be booked but not cancelled.

### 2.2 What the employee sees

`POST api/MealBooking/BookMeals` returns `Booking closed` per meal, with the deadline that was
missed spelled out as a date:

```
Ordering for this meal closed at 09:30 AM on 25 Oct 2026.
```

`POST api/MealBooking/CancelMeals` returns `Too late` the same way:

```
This meal can no longer be cancelled - ordering closed at 09:30 AM on 25 Oct 2026.
```

Deadlines are evaluated in **the canteen's own time zone** (branch entry, then company entry, then
`DefaultTimeZoneId`), not the phone's — an employee travelling abroad gets the canteen's deadline.
The boundary is inclusive: an order placed exactly at 09:30:00 still counts.

### 2.3 What HR sees

The Meal Session form has an **Ordering deadline** section with two fields — **Order Cutoff Time
(24-hour)** and **Cutoff Day** — and one line underneath that rewrites as they are changed:

```
ⓘ Employees will be able to order Breakfast till upto 11:59 PM, day before.
```

The line always restates the time in 12-hour with AM/PM, so a 24-hour value typed above can never be
read as the wrong half of the day (`17:00` echoes back as `05:00 PM`). On an unreachable
combination it is replaced by a warning and the save is blocked:

```
✕ 08:00 AM is after Breakfast starts at 07:30 AM. Pick an earlier time, or a day before.
```

The **Cutoff Day** list is filled from the API, not hard-coded, so `HR_CMS_Config` is the only place
that decides how far back a deadline may go. The Meal Session grid gets an **Orders Close** column
showing the same phrasing the employee's app shows.

### 2.4 Lowering the maximum does not strand a session

If an admin lowers `MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore` after sessions have been saved with a longer notice,
those sessions **keep their deadline and still save**. The value stays in that session's dropdown
and passes validation as long as nobody tries to move it *further* back. Without this, lowering the
setting would make an existing session impossible to edit at all — including its rates, which have
nothing to do with the deadline.

A missing `HR_CMS_Config` row reads as `1`, the seeded value, so a database that has not had the
config migration still shows a working screen rather than a dropdown with one choice.

## 3. API changes

**New endpoint**

```
GET api/MealSession/GetOrderCutoffDayOptions
→ { maxDaysBefore: 1,
    options: [ { value: 0, label: "Same day as the meal" },
               { value: 1, label: "1 day before the meal" } ] }
```

**New fields on existing responses** — `GetAllMealSessions`, `GetMealSessionById` and
`GetEmployeeMealRates` now carry `orderCutoffTime`, `orderCutoffDaysBefore` and a ready-made
`orderCutoffDescription` (`"11:59 PM the day before the meal"`). The mobile app should show the
description rather than build its own sentence from the two values.

**New required fields on save** — `InsertMealSession` and `UpdateMealSession` take
`orderCutoffTime` and `orderCutoffDaysBefore`. Rejections:

| Message | When |
|---|---|
| `Invalid order cutoff time.` | not `HH:mm` / `HH:mm:ss` |
| `Ordering must close by the time the meal starts (07:30). Choose an earlier time, or move the deadline to a day before the meal.` | same-day deadline after the meal starts |
| `The ordering deadline can be at most 1 day before the meal.` | further back than `MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore` |
| `The ordering deadline can be 0 to 7 days before the meal.` | outside the hard ceiling |

## 4. Where the wording lives

`MealOrderCutoff` (in `SolutionOne_Core`) is the single place that both *states* the deadline and
*computes* it. The sentence on the Meal Session screen, the text in the grid, the message the
employee's app receives and the moment `MealBookingService` actually refuses a booking all come from
there — so the rule shown and the rule enforced cannot drift apart.

## 5. Files changed

**Database** — `Migration_CanteenConfig_20261023.sql`,
`Migration_CanteenMealSessionOrderCutoff_20261023.sql`,
`Update_CanteenMealSession_OrderCutoff_20261023.sql`

**Backend** — `HrCmsMealSession`, `HrCmsConfig` (new), `HrmsystemContext`,
`ICanteenConfigRepository` / `CanteenConfigRepository` (new) + DI, `MealOrderCutoff` (new),
`MealSessionModels`, `MealSessionService`, `IMealSessionService`, `MealSessionController`,
`MealBookingService`, `MealBookingModels`, `appsettings.json`

**Frontend** — `meal-session-form.component.{ts,html,scss}`, `meal-session-list.component.ts`

**Tests** — `MealSessionOrderCutoffTests` (new), `MealBookingServiceTests`

config file and restarting the API.

A canteen does not work that way. Breakfast has to be counted the night before so the kitchen can
shop; lunch is counted the same morning. The deadline is a property of the meal, so it now lives on
the meal.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OrderCutoffTime` | `TIME(0)` NOT NULL | the clock time ordering closes |
| `OrderCutoffDaysBefore` | `INT` NOT NULL | which day that clock time falls on: `0` = the day of the meal, `1` = the day before, up to `7` |

Read together they are one deadline. Breakfast ordered "by 11:59 PM the night before" is
`23:59` + `1`. Lunch ordered "by 9:30 in the morning" is `09:30` + `0`.

Both are **NOT NULL by design** — there is no "deadline not configured" state for a meal session to
sit in, because the booking API has to be able to answer "is it too late?" for every meal, every
time.

Two CHECK constraints keep the pair meaningful:

```sql
CK_HR_CMS_MealSession_OrderCutoffDaysBefore
    CHECK ([OrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)

CK_HR_CMS_MealSession_OrderCutoffBeforeStart
    CHECK ([OrderCutoffDaysBefore] > 0 OR [OrderCutoffTime] <= [StartTime])
```

The second one is the rule that matters: **a deadline on the day of the meal can never be after the
meal starts.** Breakfast served 07:30–09:30 cannot be ordered at 08:00 that morning — the food is
already cooked. `07:30` exactly is allowed (it reads as "order before 7:30"); `07:31` is refused. A
deadline on an earlier day is always in time, whatever the clock says, so the constraint only
applies when `OrderCutoffDaysBefore = 0`.

### 1.2 `HR_CMS_Config` — new table

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfigId` | `INT` PK | always `1` |

| `CreateDate` / `CreatedById` / `ModifiedDate` / `ModifiedById` | | audit |

```sql
CK_HR_CMS_Config_MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore CHECK ([MaxOrderCutoffDaysBefore] BETWEEN 0 AND 7)
```
